newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen firm on Friday - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen firm on Friday - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices on Friday were seen steady with a firm tone, amid expectations for strong packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Hog demand Friday was expected to be strong as packers complete buying for a moderate to large Saturday slaughter to compensate for plant closings Thursday, Thanksgiving Day, the dealers said.

Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at plants Friday could range from $56.50 to $57.00 per cwt, sources there said. Illinois prices at plants were seen at $56.00 to possibly $57.00, sources said.
Indiana/Ohio hog buyers said top prices at plants in those areas could range from $56.00 to $56.50.
Pork prices at midday Wednesday were quoted mixed, with hams steady to $2.00 per cwt lower, bellies steady to $2.00 higher and loins too light to test, according to USDA.
The mixed prices lent concern that hog slaughter Saturday would be less than expected if packer operating margins slip into unprofitable territory, sources said.
